key_insight: Nonlinearity-subtracted DMD (NSDMD) uses nonlinear-term snapshots to learn a low-rank approximation of mean-flow-linearized turbulent dynamics from data.
engineering_relevance: It makes resolvent-style linear analysis of turbulent flows feasible as a post-processing step on standard DNS/LES outputs, even for complex geometries and full aircraft configurations.
method: Decompose perturbation dynamics with Navier–Stokes structure in mind
Subtract the contribution of nonlinear forcing using snapshots of nonlinear terms
Fit a low-rank operator suitable for data-driven resolvent analysis
evidence_signal: The method is demonstrated on DNS and LES data, starting with minimal channel flow and extending to a full aircraft model.
watch_item: Performance depends on the quality and availability of nonlinear-term snapshots and on how well the data capture the relevant turbulent regimes.
paper_title: Data-driven linear analysis of turbulent flows
